old.name: Cava — invented Penedès 1872
old.label: SPARKLING
old.hook: Macabeu + Xarel·lo + Parellada · méthode tradicional since 1872
old.text: Macabeu + Xarel·lo + Parellada · méthode tradicional since 1872 EUR 12–80 / bottle ESSENTIAL All day Josep Raventós i Fatjó produced the first cava bottle at Codorníu in 1872 — méthode tradicional on the indigenous Penedès grapes Macabeu, Xarel·lo and Parellada. Today: Cava (9 months on lees), Reserva (18+, raised from 15 in Jan 2022), Gran Reserva (30+), Cava de Paraje Calificado (36+, single-parcel, 2017 top tier — Recaredo Turó d'en Mota, Gramona Font de Jui, Codorníu El Tros Nou et al.). The small-producer breakaway: Corpinnat (Recaredo, Gramona, Llopart and six others left DO Cava in 2019; organic, manual, estate-grown). Where Sant Sadurní d'Anoia · Penedès

old.name: Vermut — Yzaguirre Reus 1884
old.label: APÉRITIF
old.hook: L'hora del vermut: Sunday noon, ice + orange twist + olives
old.text: L'hora del vermut: Sunday noon, ice + orange twist + olives EUR 3–7 / glass WALK-IN Apéritif noon–14:00 Commercial Catalan vermut was founded in 1884 in Reus (110 km south) by Enrique de Yzaguirre y de Basterreche — ~80 herbs and spices in a formula unchanged for 140 years. The drink is white wine fortified with wormwood, gentian, cinnamon, orange peel; sweet-and-bitter, lightly oxidised, amber-coloured, ~15–18% ABV. L'hora del vermut is the Sunday-noon ritual that defines Catalan social life: order it with ice and an orange twist, accompanied by olives, boquerones (white anchovies), and a small montadito. Sant Antoni — especially Bar Calders on Carrer del Parlament — is the current heart. Cafè Torino, the first dedicated vermut bar in Barcelona (1902), was co-designed by Gaudí. Where Sant Antoni · Born · Poble Sec

old.name: Priorat — DOQ since 2000
old.label: WINE
old.hook: Black slate llicorella · old-vine Garnatxa + Cariñena · only 2 DOQs in Spain
old.text: Black slate llicorella · old-vine Garnatxa + Cariñena · only 2 DOQs in Spain EUR 35–1,600 / bottle ESSENTIAL with red meat Dinner One of only two DOQs in Spain (the other is Rioja). The 1989 revival by René Barbier, Álvaro Palacios, Daphne Glorian, Carles Pastrana and Josep-Lluís Pérez (the 'Clos team') took the appellation from forgotten to legendary in eleven years — fastest elevation in Spanish history. The defining terroir is llicorella (black slate + quartz mica), which forces vines to send roots metres down; yields below 5 hl/ha on the best terraces. Palacios's L'Ermita — a 1.1 ha plot of old-vine Garnacha bought in 1993 — sells for €1,200–1,600, the most expensive Garnacha-based wine on earth. Climbing-tier entry: Montsant rings Priorat at half the price. Where 1h45–2h south of Barcelona

old.name: Xarel·lo — Penedès still white
old.label: WHITE
old.hook: The Catalan native white re-discovered as serious still wine
old.text: The Catalan native white re-discovered as serious still wine EUR 14–35 / bottle WALK-IN Lunch / Dinner Long dismissed as the workhorse base grape of cava, Xarel·lo (locally Pansa Blanca in Alella) is now bottled as a serious still wine by progressive producers — saline, mineral, age-worthy, oxidation-resistant. Pairs with pa amb tomàquet, salt cod, prawns. Alta Alella (Vallcirera Paraje Calificado, sauló soil), Recaredo (terroirs, biodynamic), Gramona (Mont Cau), Costador Mediterrani Terroirs (Joan Franquet, natural-wine reference, vines 60–110 years old) are the names to learn. Where Penedès · Alella (sauló soil)

old.name: Ratafia — the Catalan herbal
old.label: DIGESTIF
old.hook: 40–50 botanicals + unripe green walnuts, gathered eve of Sant Joan
old.text: 40–50 botanicals + unripe green walnuts, gathered eve of Sant Joan EUR 18–35 / bottle WALK-IN Digestif Catalonia's quintessential digestif. About 40–50 aromatic herbs (mint, lemon verbena, thyme, basil, lavender), flowers (carnation, jasmine), fruits (morello cherries, citrus peel), and spices (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg) macerated with alcohol — the defining ingredient is green (unripe) walnuts , which dye the liqueur a deep amber-brown and contribute the signature bitterness. Tradition: the botanicals are gathered on the eve of Sant Joan (24 June) , believed peak-potency. Macerated 40+ days, then sugar and alcohol added, aged in wood ~3 months. ~25–35% ABV. Serve chilled in a small ceramic cup after coffee. Where Montseny · Santa Coloma de Farners

old.name: Bar Salvatge
old.label: Gràcia — Carrer de Verdi 50
old.hook: Salvatge means 'wild', and it earns the name: a small, rustic-chic Gràcia room pouring natural and biodynamic bottles plus eight rotating barrels on tap, matched to local cheese and light plates. The staff can actually talk you through the growers.
old.text: Salvatge means 'wild', and it earns the name: a small, rustic-chic Gràcia room pouring natural and biodynamic bottles plus eight rotating barrels on tap, matched to local cheese and light plates. The staff can actually talk you through the growers. Signal Eight wines on tap straight from barrel; a Gràcia natural-wine reference. Verified open 2026 (Carrer de Verdi 50).

old.name: Bar Zim
old.label: Barri Gòtic — Carrer de la Dagueria 20
old.hook: Quite possibly the smallest wine cave in the city: a lone red sign, a heavy iron door, an arched brick vault and a dozen or so seats. The cheeses trace to the legendary Formatgeria de la Seu lineage and the short list is chosen to marry them; cash only.

old.name: Amateur Bar
old.label: Poblenou — Carrer de Llull 101
old.hook: A natural-wine bar on one of Poblenou's liveliest streets: exposed brick, a DJ booth and stacks of vinyl, biodynamic bottles from small growers and small plates to share. The kind of room you enter for one glass and leave hours later, with staff who'll walk you through the list.

(Its @amateur.cafe handle hints at daytime coffee, but that isn't confirmed.)

old.name: La Caseta del Migdia
old.label: Montjuic, behind the castle (Passeig del Migdia)
old.text: The anti-rooftop: a clifftop clearing in the pines behind Montjuic castle with deckchairs, candlelit tables, DJs on the breeze, the sea spread out below and one of the city's great sunsets. No skyline — all horizon and forest. ★ Order — A cold beer or vermut with the butifarra BBQ combo plate (verified ~15-euro grill combo; paella by pre-order) When Sunset in the warm season; reached by a 10-15 minute walk from the castle (Montjuic cable car up from Paral-lel). Open days vary (recently weekends, sometimes Wed-Fri) — check first Heads up — Not a hotel and not glamorous — a walk in the woods, casual, weather- and season-dependent, and it can close or run limited hours. Come for the setting, not for polish. Clifftop outdoor bar behind the Castell de Montjuic (Time Out + Barcelona Yellow + Driftwood Journals)

old.name: The Roof (The Barcelona EDITION)
old.label: El Born / Ciutat Vella, by Mercat de Santa Caterina
old.text: A tenth-floor garden in the sky: wood decking and accents, lush greenery and a plunge pool, lit low at night. The view lands on Santa Maria del Mar's Gothic bulk and the wavy colored roof of the Santa Caterina market. ★ Order — A signature cocktail alongside the Latin-American-meets-Asian sharing plates (specific drink not verified by name) When Sunset; tenth floor. A retractable roof keeps it running year-round Heads up — An Ian Schrager EDITION property — scene-y and pricey, and the plunge pool leans toward guests; the sharing-plate menu nudges you into a dinner spend. The Roof at The Barcelona EDITION, Ian Schrager's brand in Ciutat Vella (hotel site + The Rooftop Guide)

old.name: The Rooftop at Sir Victor
old.label: Eixample, Carrer del Rossello 265, beside Casa Mila
old.text: Wooden-decked terrace with loungers, a glittering pool and a DJ at golden hour, and a rare direct sightline to Gaudi's Casa Mila (La Pedrera) with the Sagrada Familia beyond. The design-hotel, see-and-be-seen option. ★ Order — The 'Popcorn Colada' (verified house cocktail), with the Greek-leaning Mediterranean sharing food When Open daily roughly noon-midnight; sunset into DJ hours; buzzy Heads up — Leans toward hotel guests and a scene — it gets loud and busy, so not the spot for a quiet aperitivo. Sir Victor (Sircle Collection / Design Hotels) rooftop overlooking Casa Mila (hotel site + Mr & Mrs Smith + The Rooftop Guide)

old_venue.name: Bar Marsella
tags: Reputedly Barcelona's oldest bar (1820); the city bought its building in 2013 to save it.
old_venue.why: Reputedly Barcelona's oldest bar (1820); the city bought its building in 2013 to save it.
old_venue.address: Carrer de Sant Pau, 65, El Raval, 08001 Barcelona
old_venue.verdict: The draw is the reputedly-1820 absinthe bar the city council saved in 2013 by buying its building, not a meal — there is no kitchen, only marble tables and the absinthe ritual.
old_venue.signature: Absinthe, sugar cube balanced on a fork, iced water poured till the glass clouds milky
old_venue.caveat: Not a restaurant and not for dinner — no food served, cash-leaning, heavily touristed, faded and unrenovated; opens evenings only and is known not to keep its posted hours (sources disagree on the exact open time and which day it closes), so go late and check ahead.
old_venue.person: Josep Lamiel, third-generation owner; the Lamiel family has run the bar for over a century (confirmed by Barcelona Metropolitan).

signal_chip.label: City-saved
signal_chip.full: Listed as a city point of interest by Barcelona City Council (meet.barcelona); in 2013 the council used its right of first refusal to buy the whole building (~EUR 1.1M) after 10,000+ signatures, saving the reputedly-1820 absinthe bar from closure.

bars:London Bar.brief: NEW bar card from the old venue record (old_venue): the modernista bar on Carrer Nou de la Rambla with the circus trapeze. Verify it trades in 2026 (it changed hands/reopened in the 2010s-20s? check) and founding year (1910 is usual). Labels Where · Pour · Price · Best hour.

old_venue.name: London Bar
tags: A 1910 modernista bar on Barcelona's official Ruta del Modernisme, with a circus trapeze overhead.
old_venue.why: A 1910 modernista bar on Barcelona's official Ruta del Modernisme, with a circus trapeze overhead.
old_venue.address: Carrer Nou de la Rambla, 34, Ciutat Vella (El Raval), 08001 Barcelona
old_venue.verdict: Come for the carved-mirror modernista room and the circus trapeze hung from the ceiling, not for the food — this is a landmark to drink in, not a kitchen.
old_venue.signature: A Negroni or Corpse Reviver No. 2 from the house list, drunk under the trapeze.
old_venue.caveat: Not a meal and not a hidden local secret: it opens evenings only, from around 19:30, and is closed Tuesdays; there is little real food, and the crowd runs tourist-heavy. It is also a 2018 revival — the bar closed in 2017 and the Raluy circus family reopened it, so it is not an unbroken century under one owner — and while the name says 1909 (when the premises were bought), the doors actually opened on 23 June 1910.
old_venue.person: Carlos Raluy, of the historic Raluy circus family (Circ Històric Raluy), who inherited the bar and reopened it in 2018

signal_chip.label: Modernisme
signal_chip.full: Listed on Barcelona's official Ruta del Modernisme (a City Council heritage initiative): a preserved modernista bar with its original carved-mirror cabinet and coloured-marble counter intact; opened 1910.
signal_chip.cosign: Ruta del Modernisme de Barcelona (official Barcelona City Council route)

old.name: Oblicuo Hi-Fi Bar
old.label: Gràcia — Carrer de la Riera de Sant Miquel 59
old.hook: A bespoke hi-fi system — voiced by sound designer Giorgio Di Salvo — plays to a room of craft cocktails, natural wine and artisanal sake. Guest vinyl selectors work most nights: spiritual jazz one evening, deep funk, Afrobeat or Brazilian cuts the next.

old.name: Jaç Hi-Fi Café
old.label: Eixample — Avinguda Diagonal 335
old.hook: A Mediterranean reading of the Japanese jazz kissa: a monolithic walnut bar doubles as a speaker cabinet, with custom Bloom Island speakers and vinyl shelves. Music is turned up and conversation down; specialty coffee by day gives way to evening listening across zoned rooms.

old.name: Discos Paradiso
old.label: El Raval (Carrer de Ferlandina, near MACBA)
old.hook: A bright, sharply curated record shop dealing new and second-hand vinyl with a strong electronic, leftfield and experimental bent, plus in-store sets.
old.text: A bright, sharply curated record shop dealing new and second-hand vinyl with a strong electronic, leftfield and experimental bent, plus in-store sets. It is the hub where the city's dance and experimental crowd actually crosses paths — opened in 2010 by two diggers who hunted rarities across Europe, and respected enough to be profiled internationally. Pair it with Wah Wah Discos on nearby Riera Baixa — a shop since 1992 that also runs the Wah Wah Records Supersonic Sounds reissue label (300+ titles) — for the two poles of Barcelona vinyl. Anchor Opened April 2010 on Carrer Ferlandina near MACBA; profiled in The Vinyl Factory's 'world's best record shops' series (#034) (discosparadiso.com, thevinylfactory.com).

old.name: Jamboree
old.label: Plaça Reial
old.hook: A vaulted stone basement on Plaça Reial running nightly jazz sets (typically two shows) that turn into a club later, run by the Mas i Mas group.
old.text: A vaulted stone basement on Plaça Reial running nightly jazz sets (typically two shows) that turn into a club later, run by the Mas i Mas group. It is the oldest jazz venue in Spain and a real piece of history rather than a themed bar: opened in 1960, it drew the touring greats during the years the US Sixth Fleet docked here. The room is small and genuinely atmospheric, though be aware it is now firmly on the tourist circuit and tickets reflect that. Anchor Opened 1960 by Joan Rosselló; the oldest jazz venue in Spain; hosted Chet Baker, Ornette Coleman, Dexter Gordon and Stéphane Grappelli; acquired by the Mas i Mas group in May 1993 (Europe Jazz Network, jamboreejazz.com).

old.name: 23 Robadors
old.label: El Raval (Carrer d'en Robador)
old.hook: A narrow, scruffy bar on one of the Raval's grittiest streets programming two live sets most days — jazz, funk, rock, hip-hop and its well-known weekend flamenco.
old.text: A narrow, scruffy bar on one of the Raval's grittiest streets programming two live sets most days — jazz, funk, rock, hip-hop and its well-known weekend flamenco. This is the unpolished, low-cost end of the live scene — independent since 2004, with a Wednesday jazz jam and weekend flamenco that draw working musicians rather than tour groups. It feels closer to the street than to the heritage circuit. Anchor Independent live-music bar on Carrer d'en Robador since 2004; two concerts most days, with a Wednesday jazz jam and weekend flamenco (timeout.com, 23robadors.com).

old.name: JazzSí Club (Taller de Músics)
old.label: El Raval (Carrer de Requesens)
old.hook: A tiny live room attached to the Taller de Músics school, with a different genre each night and a roughly €10 ticket that includes a drink.
old.text: A tiny live room attached to the Taller de Músics school, with a different genre each night and a roughly €10 ticket that includes a drink. It is the working engine of the city's music education rather than a venue chasing a crowd: the Wednesday jam is the school's own students, Thursday is Cuban/Latin, and Friday-Saturday is flamenco. You hear emerging players and seasoned teachers on the same small stage, cheaply. Anchor Run by the Taller de Músics (pioneering jazz/flamenco school); nightly themed program — Mon jazz, Wed student jam, Thu Cuban, Fri/Sat flamenco — around €10 with a drink (tallerdemusics.com, timeout.com).

old.name: Sala Apolo / Nitsa
old.label: Poble-sec — Carrer Nou de la Rambla 111-115
old.hook: A former 1940s dance hall near Paral·lel, now the city's landmark venue: live concerts early, then Nitsa, the electronic club night that has anchored Barcelona nightlife for decades. Two rooms (Apolo and the smaller Astin), deep sound, broad programming.

old.name: Razzmatazz
old.label: Poblenou
old.hook: The city's biggest club — five rooms under one Poblenou warehouse roof, indie to techno the same night.
old.text: The city's biggest club — five rooms under one Poblenou warehouse roof, indie to techno the same night. Opened in 2000 in a former warehouse on Carrer dels Almogàvers, its five environments (The Loft, Razz Club, Lolita, Pop Bar, Rex Room) run different sounds at once; the main hall doubles as one of Barcelona's key mid-size live-music stages. Anchor Opened 2000, Carrer dels Almogàvers 122, Poblenou.

old.name: Moog
old.label: El Raval (Carrer de l'Arc del Teatre)
old.hook: A small, dark single-room techno club, open since 1996 in the former Villa Rosa flamenco tablao — one of the city's first and longest-running electronic clubs, built around a Funktion-One system with sound over spectacle.
old.text: A small, dark single-room techno club, open since 1996 in the former Villa Rosa flamenco tablao — one of the city's first and longest-running electronic clubs, built around a Funktion-One system with sound over spectacle. Its value is the resident-DJ model rather than headliner culture — homegrown selectors like Omar León carry most nights, with internationals reserved for mid-week. It is the antithesis of the bottle-service club: tight, sweaty, roughly 400-capacity, dancefloor-first. Anchor Opened 21 June 1996 in the former Villa Rosa tablao; ~400 capacity on a Funktion-One system; has hosted Jeff Mills, Laurent Garnier and Richie Hawtin alongside residents like Omar León (moogbarcelona.com).

old.name: Sabor de Gràcia (rumba catalana)
old.label: Gràcia
old.hook: The standard-bearing rumba catalana band, founded by Sicus Carbonell, carrying the Gràcia gitano rumba tradition of Peret and Gato Pérez into the present.
old.text: The standard-bearing rumba catalana band, founded by Sicus Carbonell, carrying the Gràcia gitano rumba tradition of Peret and Gato Pérez into the present. Rumba catalana is the city's one truly home-grown popular music, born in the Roma quarters of Gràcia and El Raval, and Sabor de Gràcia is its most visible living thread rather than a museum act. The form is more heritage than weekly scene now, but it keeps resurfacing — which is the honest state of rumba in 2025-26. Anchor Founded 1994 by Sicus Carbonell; granted the Generalitat's Creu de Sant Jordi in May 2025 and played a free Plaça Catalunya concert in early September 2025 (beteve.cat, Wikipedia). Related anchor: Arrels de Gràcia performed Gato Pérez's 'Rumba de Barcelona' with Bad Gyal at the 2026 Goya gala in Barcelona (metropoliabierta.elespanol.com).

Labels Touch it today · Where the sources argue. No Maps unless a real place to go.

old.name: Heliogàbal
old.label: Gràcia (near Plaça Joanic)
old.hook: A tiny association-run bar-venue programming emerging and experimental music most nights, plus poetry readings, fanzine launches and exhibitions.
old.text: A tiny association-run bar-venue programming emerging and experimental music most nights, plus poetry readings, fanzine launches and exhibitions. It is the grassroots, non-commercial end of the live scene — run by a cultural association since 1995, it has launched countless local careers from a room that holds barely 66, and it won a Ciutat de Barcelona prize for music. It belongs to the same self-managed ethos as the bigger reclaimed spaces (Can Batlló, a textile complex self-run by assembly since 2011; Ateneu Popular 9 Barris, an asphalt-plant occupation since 1977 and a national reference for social circus). Anchor Run by its cultural association since 1995; capacity ~66; won the Ciutat de Barcelona award for music in 2012; marked its 30th anniversary in 2025 (heliogabal.com, timeout.com, rockdelux.com).
